3' to 5' exonuclease activity is what allows DNA polymerase to remove any mismatched bases that may be incorporated during replication. This process is called proof reading and it occurs after each addition of a nucleotide to the growing chain. Since reverse transcription does not occur on a double stranded template, HIV RNA must be converted into DNA before it can be inserted into a host cell. In order to do this, Reverse Transcriptase converts the RNA into DNA which contains many errors due to its high error rate. This prevents the virus from mutating and becoming resistant to drugs and also prevents further replication of the virus. Therefore, chemicals such as AZT are able to terminate growing viral DNA chains because REVERSE TRANSCRIPTASE DOES NOT HAVE AN INHERENT PROOF-READING FUNCTION. #### Extractive Summarization

Extractive summarization generates a summary by selecting sentences from the source text that best represent the main points of the document. Hybrid summarization combines both extractive and abstractive methods to create a summary. It selects key sentences from the original text and then uses machine learning models to generate a summary based on those sentences. This approach provides a balance between accuracy and readability, making it suitable for most types of documents.

#### Text Simplification

Text simplification makes the original text easier to understand by reducing complex words and phrases. This method works well for technical or scientific documents but may not be appropriate for creative writing or literature.
